exposure: Prenatal severity indicators (percentage observed/expected lung-to-head ratio, O/E LHR %)
outcome: Self-reported respiratory outcomes (measured by preschool respiratory outcome questionnaire and International Study of Asthma and Allergies in Childhood asthma questionnaire)
Self-reported gastrointestinal outcomes (measured by Infant Gastroesophageal Reflux Questionnaire Revised and Paediatric Gastro-oesophageal Symptom and Quality of Life Questionnaire)
cohort: Families of children prenatally diagnosed with isolated, left-sided congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH) who survived for more than 1 year.
finding: Families and children with prenatally diagnosed CDH reported fewer respiratory symptoms with increasing age, but no overall correlation was found between O/E LHR or FETO use and self-reported respiratory or gastrointestinal outcomes.
followup_time: Up to >=9 years after birth (children aged 1 to >=9 years were assessed)
